0|daa88c8d214ca4ab2f1764b6e503cef4b3cde9b2|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"[PATCH] do not disturb page referenced state when unmapping memory range
When kernel unmaps an address range
column2: it needs to transfer PTE state into

column1: page struct.  Currently
mark_page_accessed().  The call to mark_page_accessed in the unmap path
doesn't look logically correct.
At unmap time
column2: calling mark_page_accessed will causes page LRU state to be

column1: bumped up one step closer to more recently used state.  It is causing quite
a bit headache in a scenario when a process creates a shmem segment
a whole bunch of pages
column2: then unmaps it.  The unmapping takes a long time

column1: because mark_page_accessed() will start moving pages from inactive to
active list.
I'm not too much concerned with moving the page from one list to another in
LRU.  Sooner or later it might be moved because of multiple mappings from
various processes.  But it just doesn't look logical that when user asks a
range to be unmapped
column2: it's his intention that the process is no longer

column1: interested in these pages.  Moving those pages to active list (or bumping
up a state towards more active) seems to be an over reaction.  It also
prolongs unmapping latency which is the core issue I'm trying to solve.
As suggested by Peter
column2: we should still preserve the info on pte young

column1: pages
